question_text: An infinitely long thin straight wire held perpendicular to the plane of the paper at point $O$ carries a current $I$ into the paper as shown in the figure. Nine other similar infinitely long wires, parallel to the first wire and carrying the same current $I$ into the paper are placed with their centres at equal distances $r$ from $O$ as shown. Except for wire $A$ and $B$, each wire is at a distance $r$ from any two consecutive wires as in the paper. The magnitude and the direction of the magnetic force per unit length on the wire at the centre $O$ due to other wires. [Take cos 30° = $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$]

options.option_text: $\frac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r} (2+\sqrt{3})$ in the direction of YO.
$\frac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r} (1+\sqrt{3})$ in the direction of OY.
$\frac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r} (1+\sqrt{5})$ in the direction of OY.
$\frac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r} (2+\sqrt{5})$ in the direction of OX.
$\frac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r} (2-\sqrt{5})$ in the direction of YO.
